subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw implement the small safe fallback in the shared read tool now, or defer this issue to broader document extraction/provider-native file work?
rationale: Source inspection proves the token-waste path still exists, but the issue explicitly offers fallback, parser, and description-only directions; choosing which user-visible behavior belongs in core needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Ship Safe Fallback
options.body: Add a bounded detector in the current shared read tool and return a clear unsupported-document message for known binary document formats.

options.title: Defer To Extraction Work
options.body: Keep this issue open only as part of broader document parsing/provider-native file support, accepting that direct read can still waste tokens until that lands.

options.title: Description-Only Guidance
options.body: Change tool guidance without runtime blocking, which is lower risk but would not prevent accidental binary reads.

recommendation.title: Ship Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a bounded detector in the current shared read tool and return a clear unsupported-document message for known binary document formats.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared read implementation and wrapper history point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for the read-tool behavior choice.
